flash.reason: Most ESP32-C3 Super Mini boards are sold as 4 MB flash variants; verify with espflash board-info for the specific board.

uf2.reason: Generic ESP32-C3 Super Mini boards do not expose a verified UF2 bootloader by default.

GPIO2.reason: Commonly broken out on ESP32-C3 Super Mini boards, but participates in ESP32-C3 boot-mode strapping.

GPIO3.reason: Commonly broken out on ESP32-C3 Super Mini boards, but participates in ESP32-C3 boot-mode strapping.

GPIO8.reason: Common clone-board LED pin; variants may use GPIO2, GPIO7, GPIO9, or omit a controllable user LED.

GPIO9.reason: Common clone-board BOOT button pin. Holding this low during reset enters download mode on typical ESP32-C3 Super Mini boards.

console.uart0.reason: Some ESP32-C3 Super Mini boards use native USB Serial/JTAG; some expose or bridge UART0.

indicator.power_led.reason: Common ESP32-C3 Super Mini power indicator LED is not controlled by a numbered GPIO.

input.boot_button.reason: Common BOOT button is wired to GPIO9, which is also exposed on the header and acts as a boot strapping pin.

control.reset_button.reason: Common RST button pulls the ESP32-C3 enable/reset line and is not a normal GPIO breakout.

display.reason: This reference firmware target exercises headless SquidScript language behavior over serial.

storage.reason: The ESP32-C3 Super Mini reference firmware stores installed SQBC apps in a firmware-owned LittleFS partition. Content/library storage is not implemented yet.

input.reason: The ESP32-C3 Super Mini has a BOOT button, but the reference firmware uses serial commands as the primary conformance input harness.

squidscript.reason: This target exercises the initial headless SquidScript VM subset for language-spec conformance.
